extracted.intended_audience: public health communicators, national health authorities, WHO Member State outbreak communication teams
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for drafting and issuing press releases and public communications during infectious disease outbreaks, aimed at preserving credibility, informing the public, and prompting protective action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trust
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintaining the public trust must be the over-arching goal of any outbreak communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Without trust, the public will not respond to public health advice. All messaging choices should prioritize credibility and behaviors that build and preserve trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Announce Early
rubrics_metrics.description: Proactive early announcements — even with incomplete information — are essential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not delay announcing for completeness; late announcements damage credibility. Communicate early and update as information becomes available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Reveal what is known and unknown; acknowledge uncertainty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about limits of knowledge. Use language that clearly distinguishes confirmed facts from uncertainties and ongoing investigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for Public's Existing Knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Account for what the public already understands and believes; ensure cultural appropriateness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor explanations to existing beliefs, misconceptions, and cultural norms of affected populations to improve comprehension and uptake.

rubrics_metrics.name: Planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Communication should be planned in advance, not improvised during a crisis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have pre-prepared plans, roles, templates, and approval processes so communications can be issued quickly and coherently when an outbreak occurs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear statement of facts known
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a clear statement of the facts that are known about the situation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State confirmed information plainly and separately from hypotheses or evolving data so audiences can distinguish fact from speculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgment of uncertainty
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly acknowledge what is unknown or uncertain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use phrases that identify gaps and the steps being taken to resolve them; avoid giving false certainty. (‘Know what we don't know’ principle.)

rubrics_metrics.name: What the agency is doing
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe what WHO/agency is doing in response to the outbreak.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include current operational actions, investigations, resource mobilization, and plans to address the situation so the public sees active response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actionable advice for the public
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide instruction on what the public should do; give people something to do.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include clear, specific, feasible actions (behavioral steps) the public can take to reduce risk; avoid vague exhortations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where to get more information
rubrics_metrics.description: Tell audiences where they can obtain additional information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include reliable information sources, links, hotlines, and resources; make pathways to more information explicit and accessible.

rubrics_metrics.name: When next update expected / update schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: State when the next update is expected and provide an update schedule if possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide timing for follow-up communications and commit to regular updates — even if there is no new information — to maintain trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spokesperson identification and contact
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify the spokesperson and provide contact details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer a single trusted spokesperson or clearly coordinated spokespersons; include contact information for media and public inquiries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plain language
rubrics_metrics.description: Use plain language appropriate to about a Grade 6–8 reading level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid jargon and technical terms; use short sentences and familiar words to maximize comprehension across the population.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation for affected populations
rubrics_metrics.description: Translate communications for affected populations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide translations in the languages used by affected communities to ensure reach and comprehension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Make releases accessible (screen reader friendly, alt text on images).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure materials meet accessibility standards (alt text, readable formats) so people with disabilities can access the information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multilingual releases when needed
rubrics_metrics.description: Issue communications in multiple languages when required by the audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess language needs and provide multilingual materials proactively rather than reactively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordination with partner agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Release communications in coordination with other agencies and partners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate timing, content, and spokespeople with partner organizations to ensure consistency and avoid mixed messages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Express empathy
rubrics_metrics.description: Use an empathetic tone in messaging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge public fears and concerns; show understanding of hardship and loss to build rapport and receptivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistent messaging across spokespersons
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure consistency across different spokespersons and channels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Align talking points and facts among all communicators to prevent confusion and contradictory statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use multiple channels
rubrics_metrics.description: Disseminate information through multiple channels (press release + briefing + social media).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine traditional and digital channels to maximize reach; tailor format and tone to each channel while keeping content consistent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Update regularly even with no new information
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide regular updates, including when there is no new information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regular contact reassures the public and maintains trust; state explicitly that no new developments have occurred when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipate and correct misinformation
rubrics_metrics.description: Anticipate likely misinformation and correct it proactively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify common misconceptions and address them directly in communications; provide factual counterpoints and sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide context (compare to baseline risk)
rubrics_metrics.description: Place the event in context by comparing it to baseline risk or familiar references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Help audiences understand magnitude and relevance by offering comparisons, trends, or historical context to avoid misperception of risk.
